batches.purpose: Make AUZiX controllable from the desktop before chasing heavier apps: hardware probes, network settings, printers, file sharing, package health, service state, audio/session status, and container readiness.

packages.notes: First pass should be read-only Lua/TUI with JSON report output. EFL frontend follows once the probe contract settles. Panels include system health, network status/settings, packages, services, containers, desktop session, sound, printers, and SMB/NFS file sharing. Intent: packages/auzix-control-panel.intent.json
Native desktop face for the control panel; must call the same read-only probe/report backend rather than reimplementing checks.
Own desktop/operator groups for audio, video, input, storage, containers, flatpak, and package operations. This should replace ad-hoc chmod/group fixes.
Package the baseline hardware/session probes and service hooks needed for audio, power events, device discovery, and SPICE-oriented desktop validation.
Own /System/Settings/network intent, DNS/default-route probes, and future static/DHCP mutations. First pass is read-only so Control Panel can show current network state safely.
Printer service/socket/queue visibility first; add/remove printer actions require explicit privilege policy and receipts.
SMB/NFS client and share visibility first. Server/export mutations stay disabled until /System/Settings/samba and /System/Settings/nfs contracts exist.

Package-owned /Services conventions, proc/sys/dev/cgroup2/run/devpts mount expectations, service logs, and boot-time sanity checks. Carries the vmid135 Podman cgroup fix as an installable AUZiX runtime package.

batches.purpose: Install practical native tools that improve AUZiX development and pull in core dependency surfaces without jumping straight to enormous GUI stacks.

packages.notes: Provides df, du, stat, chmod/chown/chgrp, install, env, timeout, and other expected GNU userland utilities. Missing df/du/timeout already hurts diagnostics.
Own lsblk, blkid, findmnt, mount helpers, swapon, fdisk/sfdisk. Pairs with filesystem packages for Control Panel storage views.
Provides ps/top/free/uptime/sysctl style process and memory visibility; AUZiX currently lacks simple uptime/free diagnostics.
Needs exec-path helpers, templates, SSL/CA and SSH integration. Do not treat as a single command binary.
Debugger/probe tool for missing paths, syscalls, and package smoke failures.
Heavy but important. Classify dependencies first; Python support may make this a second-pass native debugger.
Small but useful for package scripts that classify ELF, images, and text payloads.
Tiny native editor baseline for installed systems without Flatpak.
Optional editor baseline and dependency probe; keep tiny variant first.
Simple GNOME text editor proof. Should force GSettings/schema, GTK source view, MIME/desktop entries, and session portal decisions.

batches.purpose: Seed normal desktop use: web, office, art, DTP, chat, and media. Use these as dependency magnets, but graduate only the packages whose receipts and runtime checks are clean.

packages.notes: Small native browser proof before Firefox/Chromium-sized closures.
Heavier browser smoke; likely reveals WebKitGTK, fonts, NSS, CA, MIME, and desktop file gaps.
Light word processor / office proof. Build script expects package id abiword.
Light spreadsheet proof. Build script expects package id gnumeric.
Vector/art dependency magnet. Consider Flatpak adapter first if native closure is too large.
Art/photo dependency magnet. Native package likely second pass after image libraries are owned.
DTP proof and font/print/PDF dependency magnet. Keep planned until Qt and font stack are cleaner.
Scoped native office proof after Control Panel: Writer/Calc launch, create document, save .odt/.ods, reopen. Java/Base/printing/export can remain second-pass.
Alternative office-suite proof if packaging closure is friendlier than LibreOffice. Keep scoped to Writer/Calc local files first.
GNOME Settings/control-panel dependency magnet. Treat as a plumbing probe, not the primary AUZiX Control Panel UX.
Password manager proof. Good for Qt runtime, desktop secrets/keyring decisions, and local encrypted-file handling.
Native EFL photo viewer/editor seed. Good AUZiX-native visual app after EFL/Enlightenment are already part of the base.
MATE text editor proof. Similar dependency pressure to gedit but usually a friendly native desktop app target.
Chat app should start as Flatpak/web wrapper; audio/session readiness must be visible in Control Panel first.
